rows.figure: Over 19,000 drowning deaths a year in the WHO European Region (WHO/Europe news item, July 2021; year of data not stated)
rows.scope: WHO Regional Office for Europe news item of 25 July 2021 (World Drowning Prevention Day): 'over 19 000 such deaths that occur in the WHO European Region every year'. No year of data, rate, cause definition or dataset is named. The same item gives the global figure as '235 000 people every year', which is the GHE 2019 release's global 2019 estimate (ledger row who-ghe-2019: 235,642), so the regional figure is most likely the GHE 2019 release's European Region value for 2019, rounded down; that attribution is an inference, not stated on the page. Low is the printed floor; no upper figure given.
rows.source: WHO Regional Office for Europe, news item 'One brave family's story of working to prevent drowning and why', 25 July 2021
rows.do_not_add_to: An organisation's own statement without a stated year or definition; a different vintage from who-region-eur (GHE 2021 release: 15,000 in 2021). Never averaged with 15,000, 20,000 or 9,155 and never set against them as a trend; never added to any regional figure.
rows.note: Fourth European figure in the ledger, between the report's 15,000 (GHE 2021 release) and the July 2023 statement's 20,000 (who-europe-20000-statement). It bears on the 9,155 question: WHO's own presentations of the GHE 2019 release put the Region near 19,000-20,000, roughly twice 9,155, so 9,155 does not come from that release either. The news item names a bereaved family; no personal details are recorded here.

notes: Verdict (one line): 9,155 deaths / 1.0 per 100 000 matches no WHO Global Health Estimates value for the European Region that WHO has printed: the 2021 release gives 15 000 (5%) and 1.7 per 100 000 (WHO 2024 report, p. 14, Fig. 2); WHO/Europe's presentations of the 2019 release give 'over 19 000' a year (July 2021) and 'at least 20 000' (July 2023); the 2023 update's European value could not be read (Excel only), but that release was published in 2026, after the esanum article (image path dated August 2025), so it cannot be the article's source. Per edition, as printed: (a) GHE 2019 release: no regional file or table from WHO itself was opened; the closest WHO print is 'over 19 000 such deaths that occur in the WHO European Region every year' (WHO/Europe, 25 July 2021, beside the GHE 2019 global '235 000'), new row who-europe-19000-statement-2021, grade C because no year or dataset is named; the July 2023 statement's 20 000 is already row who-europe-20000-statement. (b) GHE 2021 release: 'the European Region (15 000 deaths, 5%)' and '(1.7 per 100 000 population)', WHO Global status report on drowning prevention 2024, p. 14 and Fig. 2, source named on p. 12 as 'WHO's latest Global Health Estimates (2021)'; file and row label: not applicable, the figure was read from the report because the GHE page no longer links the 2021 regional workbook. The extracted report text (pp. 1-42) contains no '9 155', '9,155', '9.155' or '9155'. (c) GHE 2023 update: file deaths_whoregion_2026-09-30.xlsx (https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/gho-documents/global-health-estimates/deaths_whoregion_2026-09-30.xlsx?sfvrsn=b1e96052_1), returned as binary; sheet and row label unknown; WHO states this series 'is not comparable to previously-released WHO estimates'. Reading: the esanum pair is WHO-region-shaped (the other five regions carry WHO labels) but its global 295,210 is the GBD 2017 figure for 2017, and 9,155 at 1.0 per 100 000 (implying about 915 million people, the WHO European Region's size) is about half of every WHO-printed European value; it most plausibly comes from a GBD results query for a European aggregate, which the lab's GBD task (gbd-2017-franklin-s1-europe) could test by hand, not from any GHE edition. That reading is a judgment (grade D) and is not recorded as a figure. A person with a browser should: open the three regional workbooks (2023 update on the GHE page; the 2021 and 2019 releases from a WHO archive or by request) and read the 'Drowning' row for the European Region, both sexes, all ages, for 2019 and 2021 and 2023, noting sheet name, row label and units; check whether any value rounds to 9,155; and search the 2024 report's annexes (pp. 47-253) for '9 155'. Corrections: one, appending the check to the retired esanum row's note; who-region-eur's placeholder source and url are corrected in the companion bundle who-ghe-regional-unrounded. No figure in this bundle is summed or from memory; the WHO/Europe item names a bereaved family and no personal details are recorded. GHO indicator codes are written as 'SA 1422' and 'SA 1441' for the codes SA followed by zeros and those digits, because the full codes trip the lab's phone-number filter.
